name: California
note: In California the funeral director registers the death with the local registrar through CA-EDRS within 8 calendar days, and before disposition. The attending physician certifies the cause within 15 hours, or the coroner does so for reportable deaths. Registration gates the disposition permit. Authorized certified copies are restricted, but informational copies are available to anyone. Deaths flow from the registrar to county elections officials. Federal benefit agencies are reached through the State's EDR feed to SSA (federal layer). None of this could be checked against the statute text in this pass because the official code host blocked the session.

citations.title: Registration of death within 8 calendar days and before disposition
Funeral director's duty to complete and register the death certificate
Medical certification by the physician within 15 hours
Deaths to be reported to the coroner
Coroner's duty to inquire into and determine circumstances of death
Permit for disposition of human remains
Authorized certified copies; informational certified copies
Notice of deceased persons to the county elections official

steps.title: Death determined under the Uniform Determination of Death Act
steps.who: A physician (or other person authorised to pronounce) determining death by cessation of circulatory and respiratory, or of all brain, functions.
steps.summary: California adopts the Uniform Determination of Death Act. The place where death is officially pronounced sets the registration district.

steps.title: Informant supplies personal particulars to the funeral director
steps.who: Next of kin or another informant.
steps.summary: The funeral director gathers the decedent's personal data from an informant to complete the certificate.

steps.title: Attending physician completes the medical certification within 15 hours
steps.summary: The physician completes and attests the medical and health section and the time of death within 15 hours after the death, unless the coroner must be notified.

steps.title: Reportable deaths go to the coroner
steps.who: The physician, funeral director or other person with knowledge of a reportable death.
steps.trigger: A death in a category the coroner must investigate (violent, sudden or unusual, unattended, and so on).
steps.summary: The Health and Safety Code lists the deaths to be reported to the coroner, and the Government Code makes it the coroner's duty to inquire into and determine their circumstances, manner and cause.

steps.title: Coroner completes the medical certification
steps.who: The county coroner or medical examiner.
steps.summary: In coroner cases the coroner, not the attending physician, completes the cause-of-death section of the certificate.

steps.title: Funeral director registers the death with the local registrar within 8 calendar days
steps.who: The funeral director (or the person acting as one) in charge of the remains.
steps.trigger: Completion of the certificate; before disposition.

deadline.text: within 8 calendar days after death and prior to any disposition

steps.summary: Each death must be registered with the local registrar of births and deaths for the district where death was pronounced or the body was found, within 8 calendar days after death and before any disposition. Registration is done through the California Electronic Death Registration System (CA-EDRS).

steps.title: Local registrar issues the disposition permit
steps.who: The local registrar of births and deaths.
steps.summary: A permit for disposition is issued once the certificate is registered, so registration gates burial or cremation.

steps.title: Authorized certified copies are restricted; informational copies are open
steps.who: The State Registrar or a local registrar or county recorder.
steps.trigger: Application, with a sworn statement for an authorized copy.
steps.summary: Only listed persons (close relatives, legal representatives, funeral directors, certain agencies, people with a court order) may obtain an authorized certified copy. Anyone else gets an informational certified copy marked as not valid to establish identity.

steps.title: Registrar notifies the county elections official of deceased persons
steps.who: The local registrar of births and deaths (or county health officer).
steps.trigger: Registration of deaths of persons of voting age.
steps.summary: Deaths are reported monthly to the county elections official, who cancels the affidavits of registration of deceased voters.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Within 8 calendar days after death and before disposition (not verified against the statute text in this pass).

informantDuty.note: The funeral director completes and registers the certificate; the informant only supplies particulars.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of ordinary certificates; the coroner sees only reportable deaths.

electronicRegistration.note: Statewide CA-EDRS, used by funeral directors, physicians and coroners. The statutory basis was not confirmed.

certificateAccess.note: Authorized certified copies only to listed persons on a sworn statement; informational certified copies (marked as not valid to establish identity) to anyone.

gaps: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov answered every request (curl and WebFetch, several URL forms) with a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' challenge (HTTP 403), an anti-automation control, so no California statute text could be read. law.cornell.edu (the allowed mirror) was refused at the egress proxy. All steps and features rest on recollection of the codes and are marked unverified; section numbers need confirming from the text.

CDPH (cdph.ca.gov), DHCS (Medi-Cal), the Secretary of State and the DMV were all blocked at the egress proxy. Agency guidance on CA-EDRS, the statutory or regulatory basis for electronic registration, and California's EDR feed to SSA under 42 U.S.C. 405(r) could not be sourced.

No California provision was found or verified for death notification to the DMV, the Franchise Tax Board or Medi-Cal (DHCS). The Medi-Cal estate recovery notice duty (Prob. Code 9202) was not checked in this pass.
The exact deadline for the coroner's certification (believed to be 3 days after examination under HSC 102860) and the list of reportable deaths in HSC 102850 were not read.
Elections Code 2205's exact sender (local registrar or State Registrar) and timing were not confirmed. California's statewide VoteCal list maintenance with CDPH death data was not sourced.
